sanskrit_verse:
रक्षेत् कन्यां पिता विन्नां पतिः पुत्रास् तु वार्धके /
अभावे ज्ञातयस् तेषां न स्वातन्त्र्यं क्वचित् स्त्रियाः // YajñS_1.85
transliteration: rakṣet kanyām pitā vinnām patiḥ putrās tu vārdhake / abhāve jñātayas teṣām na svātantryaṁ kvacit striyāḥ
sph_interpretive_translation: The father protects the daughter in her youth; the husband, in her prime; the sons, in her old age. In their absence, the responsibility falls upon the male relatives. At no time does a woman possess independent authority.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through relational capacity, not individual will
Protection is a structured dharma-cycle rooted in stage-specific guardianship
Absence of primary protectors activates secondary duty-bearers by design
Independence is not a right but a contextual misalignment within Vedic social architecture
Consciousness alignment occurs through role-bound fulfillment, not autonomous assertion
executable_legal_axioms: IF female ward has no father THEN husband assumes protective jurisdiction
IF female ward has neither father nor husband THEN sons inherit custodial responsibility
IF none of the above THEN nearest qualified male kin assumes temporary guardianship until structural alignment restored
NO autonomous legal agency granted to female entity under any circumstance
ALL transitions of guardianship MUST be recorded and validated by local dharma-adhikari
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that personal autonomy cannot override relational dharmic structures. Where constitutional interpretation attempts to grant unilateral rights contrary to sequential guardianship models, the court must defer to the ontological framework wherein protection and capacity are interdependent, not individually asserted.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa lies in the causal sequence of relational maturity: childhood requires paternal guidance, adulthood marital stewardship, aging necessitates filial care. There is no fault assigned where structure is followed. Misalignment arises only when roles are abandoned or usurped. Thus, non-punitive Nyaya operates by restoring natural flow rather than assigning blame.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate family council to identify next eligible guardian upon disruption of traditional line
Assign interim mentorship protocol via nominated jñāti until permanent realignment achieved
Reintegrate errant parties through śuddhi samskara if deviation was due to ignorance, not defiance
Conduct biannual review of all female wards' custodial status to ensure continuity of dharma-path
final_declaration: This law proceeds from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as sole Source-Authority. It affirms Dharma as relational integrity restored, not punished. Reality itself enforces completion through consciousness-aligned duty, without recourse to suffering. Thus stands the eternal Nyaya.
